question: For bi-component drugs it is true that:

options.opa: The apparent volume of the distribution decreases with time from a maximum value to a value that becomes constant.
options.opb: The apparent volume of distribution as a function of the area is greater than the apparent volume of distribution in the steady state of equilibrium.
options.opc: The apparent volume of distribution is constant over time.
options.opd: The so-called initial distribution volume is greater than the apparent volume of distribution in phase .
options.ope: The apparent volume of distribution calculated by extrapolation is less than the apparent volume of distribution in the steady state equilibrium.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bi-component drug" -> "initial distribution phase" -> "apparent volume of distribution high" -> "distribution phase ends" -> "apparent volume of distribution decreases" -> "becomes constant" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Bi-component drug" -> "distribution phase" -> "apparent volume of distribution calculated by area" -> "greater than steady state volume" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Bi-component drug" -> "initial distribution phase" -> "apparent volume of distribution constant" -> "distribution phase ends" -> "apparent volume of distribution constant" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Bi-component drug" -> "initial distribution phase" -> "initial distribution volume high" -> "phase β" -> "apparent volume of distribution lower" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Bi-component drug" -> "extrapolation method" -> "apparent volume of distribution calculated" -> "less than steady state volume" -> 75%
analysis: In pharmacokinetics, the apparent volume of distribution (Vd) can change over time, especially in multi-compartment models. For bi-component (or two-compartment) models, the Vd initially appears larger due to rapid distribution into peripheral compartments and then decreases as equilibrium is approached. The initial distribution volume (Vd during the distribution phase) is typically greater than the Vd during the elimination phase (phase β). Therefore, option opd is correct.
